subject: ela
skillName: Use technology to produce and publish writing
intro: Writers use technology to produce, publish, and share their work, and to collaborate with others. In each item, read the short scenario, message, comment, or draft excerpt provided, then decide which choice best fits the writer's purpose and audience. Everything you need is included in the item.

items.prompt: Read the scenario: 'You are writing a three-page research report for class. You want readers to find the Introduction, Methods, and Results sections quickly as they scroll. You also want each section title to look the same.' Which word-processing choice best serves this purpose: highlighting each title in a different color, applying a Heading style to each section title, underlining the first word of each section, or increasing the spacing before each paragraph?
items.answer: Applying a Heading style to each section title, because heading styles label and separate the sections so readers can scan and jump to them, and they keep every section title formatted consistently.

steps: Identify the purpose: readers need to find three named sections quickly, and the titles should look uniform.
Heading styles label each section and can be listed in a navigation pane, so readers can scan and jump to a section.
Heading styles also apply the same formatting to every title, meeting the consistency goal.
Different highlight colors and underlining a single word are decoration that does not organize sections; extra spacing adds gaps but does not label the sections.
The best choice is applying a Heading style to each section title.

items.prompt: Read the draft sentence: 'Our team will meat at the library to finish the slideshow.' You run spell check and it reports no spelling errors. Which statement is correct: the sentence is fine because spell check found nothing, 'meat' should be 'meet' and spell check missed it because 'meat' is spelled correctly, 'library' should be capitalized, or 'slideshow' should be two words?
items.answer: 'Meat' should be 'meet' and spell check missed it because 'meat' is spelled correctly, so the writer must catch this real-word error themselves.

steps: Read the sentence for meaning: the team will gather, which is 'meet,' not 'meat,' the food.
Spell check flags words that are spelled wrong, but 'meat' is a correctly spelled word, so it passes the check.
This is a real-word error that the writer must catch by reading carefully.
The sentence is not fine, 'library' does not need a capital here, and 'slideshow' is acceptable as one word, so those options are wrong.
The correct fix is 'meat' to 'meet.'

items.prompt: Read the comment a student left on a classmate's shared draft about ocean pollution: 'I guess it is okay.' The goal of a peer comment is to help the writer improve. Rewrite this comment so it is specific, respectful, and useful.
items.answer: A strong rewrite is: 'Your opening fact about plastic in the ocean is interesting, but the third paragraph would be stronger if you added an example of how pollution harms sea animals.' It names a specific part, stays respectful, and suggests a concrete improvement.

steps: Identify why the original is weak: 'I guess it is okay' is vague, points to nothing specific, and gives the writer no way to improve.
A useful comment names a specific part of the draft so the writer knows where to look.
It stays respectful and on topic rather than harsh or off subject.
It suggests one concrete improvement, such as adding an example or evidence.
The rewrite above names the third paragraph, stays kind, and asks for a specific example, so it meets all three goals.

items.prompt: Read the scenario: 'You found a useful sentence on a science website: "Honeybees can visit up to five thousand flowers in one day." You want to use this fact in your report.' Which choice is the most responsible way to use it: copy the sentence exactly with no mention of the site, put the fact in your own words and name the website as your source, change two words and call it your own, or leave the fact out so you do not have to credit anyone?
items.answer: Put the fact in your own words and name the website as your source, because paraphrasing and crediting the source uses the information honestly and avoids plagiarism.

steps: The goal is to use the fact honestly without plagiarizing.
Paraphrasing puts the idea in your own words, and naming the source gives credit to where the fact came from.
Copying the sentence with no credit is plagiarism, and changing only two words while claiming it as your own is still plagiarism.
Leaving out a useful, relevant fact is not necessary and weakens the report.
The responsible choice is to paraphrase and name the source.

items.prompt: Read the scenario: 'You need to ask the school principal for permission to use the gym after school for a study club. Your message should be formal and go directly to one reader.' Which digital tool fits best: a public post on the class blog, a formal email to the principal, a group text to your friends, or a comment on the school's social media page?
items.answer: A formal email to the principal, because email reaches one specific reader directly and supports the respectful, formal tone a request to a school leader needs.

steps: Identify the purpose and audience: a formal request sent to one specific person, the principal.
A formal email goes directly to that one reader and supports a polite, formal tone.
A public blog post and a social media comment are seen by many readers and are not private or formal enough for a direct request.
A group text to friends does not reach the principal at all.
The best tool is a formal email to the principal.

items.prompt: Read the comment on your shared document from a group member: 'Could you add a source for the statistic in paragraph two?' Which response best moves the writing forward: deleting the comment, replying 'Stop telling me what to do,' replying 'Good catch, I will add the link to the study I used,' or ignoring it and moving on?
items.answer: Replying 'Good catch, I will add the link to the study I used,' because it accepts a useful suggestion and states a clear next step to improve the writing.

steps: The comment is a helpful, on-topic request to support a statistic with a source.
A strong response accepts the feedback and names what you will do about it.
'Good catch, I will add the link' accepts the suggestion and gives a clear next step.
Deleting or ignoring the comment leaves the writing unimproved, and 'Stop telling me what to do' is defensive and unkind.
The best response is to accept the feedback and state the next step.

items.prompt: Read the scenario: 'In your report you have a list of five supplies a reader should bring on a field trip. Right now the supplies are written in one long sentence separated by commas, and readers keep skimming past items.' Which formatting feature best helps readers see each supply clearly: making the whole sentence bold, turning the items into a bulleted list, increasing the font size of the whole report, or changing the page margins?
items.answer: Turning the items into a bulleted list, because a bulleted list separates each supply onto its own line so readers can see and check off every item.

steps: Identify the purpose: readers should easily see each of the five separate supplies.
A bulleted list places each item on its own line, making the items easy to scan and count.
Making the sentence bold or enlarging the whole report changes appearance but still leaves the items crammed in one sentence.
Changing the margins does not separate the items either.
The best feature is a bulleted list.

items.prompt: Read the draft sentence: 'The students brought there own laptops to class.' Spell check shows no errors. Which correction is needed: the sentence is correct as written, 'there' should be 'their,' 'brought' should be 'brung,' or 'laptops' should be 'laptop's'?
items.answer: 'There' should be 'their,' because the laptops belong to the students, so the possessive 'their' is needed, and spell check missed it since 'there' is spelled correctly.

steps: Read for meaning: the laptops belong to the students, which calls for the possessive word 'their.'
'There' refers to a place, so it is the wrong word here, even though it is spelled correctly.
Spell check accepts 'there' because it is a real word, so the writer must catch this real-word error.
'Brung' is not standard English, and 'laptop's' would be a wrong possessive for a plural, so those options are incorrect.
The correct fix is 'there' to 'their.'

items.prompt: Read the scenario: 'Your class is writing one report together, and four students need to add paragraphs, see each other's changes, and leave notes for one another as they work.' Which digital tool fits this purpose best: each student emailing a separate copy to the teacher, a shared online document everyone can edit and comment in, one student typing alone in a private file, or posting drafts on a public blog?
items.answer: A shared online document everyone can edit and comment in, because it lets all four students add to the same draft, see each other's changes, and leave notes for one another.

steps: Identify the purpose: several students writing together on one report and leaving notes for each other.
A shared online document lets everyone edit the same file, see changes, and use comments to communicate.
Emailing separate copies creates many versions that are hard to combine.
One student working alone in a private file shuts out the group, and a public blog is for publishing, not for collaborative drafting.
The best tool is a shared online document.

items.prompt: Read the scenario: 'You are about to publish your personal essay on the class blog, which anyone on the internet can read.' Which choice shows the most responsible online conduct: including your home address so readers can mail you, using a respectful tone and leaving out private personal details, adding an unkind remark about a classmate to be funny, or posting a friend's phone number?
items.answer: Using a respectful tone and leaving out private personal details, because protecting personal information and keeping a respectful tone keeps publishing safe and considerate.

steps: The essay will be public, so safety and respect matter.
Leaving out private details like addresses and phone numbers protects personal information.
Keeping a respectful tone protects you and others from harm.
Posting your home address, an unkind remark, or a friend's phone number all share private information or are disrespectful.
The responsible choice is a respectful tone with no private personal details.

items.prompt: Read the two comments left on a classmate's draft. Comment 1: 'Great work, do not change anything.' Comment 2: 'Your introduction grabbed my attention, but the conclusion ends suddenly, so try adding a sentence that sums up your main point.' Which comment is more useful for helping the writer revise, and why?
items.answer: Comment 2 is more useful, because it praises a specific part, names a specific weakness in the conclusion, and suggests a concrete fix, while Comment 1 is vague praise that gives the writer nothing to improve.

steps: Compare the two comments by how much they help the writer revise.
Comment 1 is vague praise; 'do not change anything' gives no specific guidance and no path to improve.
Comment 2 points to a specific strength (the introduction) and a specific problem (the abrupt conclusion).
Comment 2 also suggests a concrete fix: add a sentence that sums up the main point.
Because it is specific, respectful, and actionable, Comment 2 is the more useful comment.

items.prompt: Read the scenario: 'You want to type a three-page story in one class period without your hands getting tired or your speed dropping.' Which habit best supports steady, accurate keyboarding: looking at the keys and typing with one finger, resting your fingers on the home row and keeping a steady rhythm, hitting each key as hard as you can, or stopping to reread after every single word?
items.answer: Resting your fingers on the home row and keeping a steady rhythm, because home-row touch typing builds the speed and stamina needed to type several pages in one sitting.

steps: Identify the goal: type several pages in one sitting with steady speed and without tiring.
Home-row touch typing lets your fingers move efficiently and keep a steady rhythm.
This habit builds the speed and stamina to type a multi-page piece at once.
One-finger hunt-and-peck is slow, hitting keys hard tires the hands, and stopping after every word breaks your flow.
The best habit is resting on the home row with a steady rhythm.

items.prompt: Read the scenario: 'For a report on healthy eating, you find two websites. Site A is a hospital's nutrition page that lists its authors and the date it was updated. Site B is an anonymous personal blog with no author named and no date.' Which source is more credible for facts in your report, and what should you do when you use it?
items.answer: Site A, the hospital's nutrition page, is more credible because it names its authors and shows an update date, and you should paraphrase the facts in your own words and credit the site as your source.

steps: Compare credibility: a hospital page that names authors and shows a recent date is more trustworthy than an anonymous, undated blog.
Named authors, an organization, and a date are signs the information is reliable and current.
Site B gives no author and no date, so its facts cannot be verified as easily.
When using Site A, paraphrase the facts in your own words and name the source to avoid plagiarism.
Site A is the more credible source, and you should credit it when you use it.

items.prompt: Read the scenario: 'In your essay, you have a key term that appears in one paragraph: the word "photosynthesis." Your teacher asks you to make that one word stand out within the sentence so a reader notices it, without changing any other text.' Which formatting feature fits best: putting the whole paragraph in a heading style, making the single word bold, changing the page to landscape orientation, or adding a bulleted list?
items.answer: Making the single word bold, because bold formatting emphasizes one important word within a sentence so a reader notices it without changing the rest of the text.

steps: Identify the purpose: emphasize one key word within a sentence, leaving everything else the same.
Bold formatting makes a single word stand out from the surrounding text.
A heading style is for section titles, not for emphasizing one word inside a paragraph.
Changing the page orientation and adding a bulleted list affect layout, not the emphasis of one word.
The best feature is making the single word bold.

items.prompt: Read the scenario: 'You wrote a paragraph that says "the cat" in fourteen places, and you decide to change every "the cat" to "the kitten" throughout the document quickly and consistently.' Which word-processing feature best does this: rereading and retyping each one by hand, using Find and Replace, changing the font of the paragraph, or running spell check?
items.answer: Using Find and Replace, because it locates every instance of 'the cat' and swaps it for 'the kitten' quickly and consistently across the whole document.

steps: Identify the task: change the same phrase in many places quickly and without missing any.
Find and Replace searches the whole document for the phrase and replaces every match at once.
Retyping each one by hand is slow and risks missing some, which breaks consistency.
Changing the font does not change the words, and spell check looks for misspellings, not for a phrase to swap.
The best feature is Find and Replace.
